discrepancyAnalysis.likelyCause: The $11,039.67 discrepancy equals exactly the Gift-In-Kind Income deducted from operating activities (Account 4012: $11,039.67). Gift-in-kind transactions may have increased asset values (e.g., donated equipment recorded to 1300 Woodworking Shop Assets) without a corresponding cash inflow. If donated assets were recorded as both income and fixed assets, the capital expenditure figure in investing activities would be overstated by the non-cash portion. Alternatively, if gift-in-kind was recorded only to income with no asset entry, the deduction from operating activities is correct and the discrepancy may reflect other unidentified non-cash transactions or timing items not captured in the balance sheet comparison.
recommendedActions: Verify whether Gift-In-Kind donations were recorded as fixed asset additions in account 1300. If so, reduce capital expenditures in investing activities by $11,039.67 (non-cash investing activity — disclose in footnotes per ASC 230).
Review whether the $40,214.92 increase in Shop Assets (1300) includes non-cash gift-in-kind additions. If $11,039.67 of that increase is non-cash, cash capex = $29,175.25.
Confirm Northwestern Mutual account classification (cash equivalent vs. investment) as this affects both beginning/ending cash and investing activities.

partI_summary.missionStatement: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild promotes the art and craft of woodworking through education, skill-building programs, and community engagement. The Guild provides members access to shop facilities, tools, safety training, and educational events to advance woodworking knowledge and craftsmanship.

partIII_programServiceAccomplishments.missionStatement: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild promotes the art and craft of woodworking through education, skill-building programs, and community engagement. The Guild provides members access to shop facilities, tools, safety training, and educational events to advance woodworking knowledge and craftsmanship.

programServices.description: Occupancy and facility operations: The Guild maintained and operated its woodworking shop facility at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO, providing members with access to professional-grade woodworking equipment, shop space, and tools. Facility costs include rent, utilities, and maintenance necessary to support all member programs.

Woodworking skills and safety education: The Guild offered hands-on woodworking skills classes (4002, $72,665 revenue) and safety education courses (4003, $9,400 revenue) to members and the public. Expenses include instructor costs, materials, and merchant processing fees for skills education ($52,553) and safety education ($4,032).

Depreciation of shop assets and leasehold improvements: The Guild recorded depreciation on woodworking shop equipment and leasehold improvements used exclusively in program service delivery. Shop assets depreciation $55,727 less prior accumulated; leasehold improvements depreciation $26,286 less prior accumulated; total current-year depreciation $48,323.56.

Other program services including program events ($14,232 expense; $8,614 revenue), membership support ($12,475 expense; $253,606 revenue included in 4a), merchandise ($6,210 expense; $3,825 revenue), storage ($11,778 revenue), library ($206 revenue), assets sold ($7,359 revenue), other program income ($7,257 revenue), rent income ($39,349 revenue), and insurance ($15,105 expense).

scheduleO.narrative: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild Inc (KCWG) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization founded in 1992 and incorporated in Missouri. The Guild's mission is to promote the art and craft of woodworking through education, skill-building programs, and community engagement. The Guild provides members with access to a shared woodworking shop facility equipped with professional-grade tools and equipment, offers woodworking skills and safety education classes, hosts program events and special events, and maintains a library of woodworking resources. The Guild also facilitates storage services, merchandise sales, and facility rental to mission-aligned users. All activities are directed toward advancing woodworking knowledge and craftsmanship among members and the broader community.

The organization relies substantially on volunteer labor to operate its shop facility, deliver educational programming, and administer member services. The total number of volunteers is not tracked in a formal system; management estimates the organization engages volunteers throughout the year. A precise count is unavailable from QuickBooks or WildApricot data for this reporting period.

scheduleO.partAndLine: Part I Line 12 — Tax Year Note
scheduleO.narrative: This Form 990 covers an 18-month period from January 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. The organization should confirm with its tax advisor whether IRS approval has been obtained for this non-standard fiscal year or whether this constitutes a short-period return requiring a separate filing election.

Occupancy and facility operations represent the largest program service expense category at $270,168.81. This includes rent expense (account 5005, $230,819.81) and facilities maintenance (account 5015, $12,172.45), shop equipment maintenance (account 5014, $10,255.65), shop supplies (account 5016, $7,409.60), and A/V equipment (account 5009, $1,094.02), all allocated 100% to program services. The Guild's facility at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO serves as the primary location for all member programs and educational activities.

Woodworking skills and safety education expenses totaled $56,585.48, comprising skills education expenses (account 5001, $52,553.09 including merchant fees $4,228.21) and safety education expenses (account 5002, $4,032.39 including merchant fees $506.14). Revenue from these programs was $82,065.00 ($72,665.00 skills education and $9,400.00 safety education). These programs are central to the Guild's educational mission.

The organization reported gross fundraising event income of $90,955.45 (account 4101 Fundraising Projects Income) on Part VIII Line 8a, which exceeds the $15,000 Schedule G threshold. Schedule G (Supplemental Information Regarding Fundraising or Gaming Activities) should be completed. Direct expenses attributable to fundraising events were not separately isolated in QuickBooks; the preparer should allocate applicable costs from account 5003 Woodworking Program Events Expense to Part VIII Line 8b and Schedule G.

The Form 990 is reviewed by the Treasurer and presented to the governing body prior to filing. Board members are provided a copy of the completed return for review and approval before submission to the IRS.

The organization does not currently have a formal written conflict of interest policy. Management should consider adopting a written conflict of interest policy consistent with IRS best practices for 501(c)(3) organizations.

The organization makes its governing documents and financial statements available to the public upon written request directed to the Treasurer at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO 64108-1121. The organization's Form 990 is also available through the IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search database.
